 Farmers in southern Vietnam to get support selling products on Amazon, Shopee, TikTok Shop 
 Vietnam's southern provinces and cities have stepped up trade promotion to expand market access for local businesses, with the Vietnam E-commerce and Digital Economy Agency set to help them list products on major e-commerce platforms and expand online exports. 
 Many localities in Vietnam have chosen to promote and sell their products on e-commerce platforms. Photo: Quang Dinh / Tuoi Tre
 Southern provinces boost e-commerce
 According to a report by the industry and trade sector, Can Tho City organized 10 domestic trade promotion programs.
 The programs connected products under the One Commune One Product (OCOP) initiative and outstanding rural industrial products with international retail chains, including Aeon, Walmart, Central Group, Lotte, and Mega Market.
 Vinh Long Province organized four trade fairs and participated in 17 interprovincial product showcase events.
 The province also prepared 30 local specialty products for promotion in South Korea.

 In Ca Mau Province, trade fairs and exhibitions organized by traders brought together around 4,300 businesses and more than 4,000 booths.
 The events attracted 645,000 visits and generated more than VND72 billion (US$2.74 million) in revenue.
 Ho Chi Minh City led interprovincial supply-demand connection programs.
 The city also stepped up operations of its pork trading platform.
 Dong Thap Province connected two tra fish (pangasius) farming areas that met required standards with the Saigon Union of Trading Cooperatives (Saigon Co.op) for distribution.
 The province also helped My Phong Cooperative bring its green-skin pomelos to more major supermarket shelves.
 Dong Thap organized five live-stream sales sessions on TikTok Shop and Shopee to expand online retail activities.
 The sessions supported 32 new sellers, attracted more than 6.5 million views, and generated 3,380 orders.
 A live-stream sale held directly at a pineapple farm in Hung Thanh Commune generated 1,000 orders, equivalent to 3.5 tonnes of pineapples.
 Ca Mau organized seven training courses for small traders on live-stream selling, pricing, and artificial intelligence applications.
 The province also helped 56 OCOP producers list 110 products on Buudien.vn.
 Agency to help businesses access major e-commerce platforms
 Le Hoang Oanh, director of the Vietnam E-commerce and Digital Economy Agency. Photo: Thy Nhung
 Le Hoang Oanh, director of the Vietnam E-commerce and Digital Economy Agency, discussed regional e-commerce cooperation plans for 2026-30 at the 12th Conference of Industry and Trade Sectors of Southern Provinces and Cities in 2026.
 She said the agency was ready to help the southern provinces and cities develop an e-commerce ecosystem, which covers e-commerce platforms, logistics infrastructure, and digital payment solutions.
 The agency has worked closely with Amazon, Shopee, and TikTok to expand online exports.
 Oanh called on provincial and municipal departments of industry and trade to review local businesses and compile lists of businesses and products that meet the required standards.
 The agency would use the lists to help eligible businesses list their products on international e-commerce platforms.
 The agency has issued export guides for India, China, Japan, and South Korea.
 It plans to release in-depth guides to the U.S. and Chinese markets in the fourth quarter.
 Sellers on e-commerce platforms in Vietnam will also be required to verify their identities. Photo: Tuoi Tre
 Under Project 06, the agency has begun connecting data from e-commerce platforms to extract sales and order figures by locality.
 Two localities are ready to participate in the data connection, while 10 others have registered.
 In October 2026, the agency plans to strengthen data integration with tax and customs authorities.
 The integration is intended to improve the tracking of goods flows and revenue from online exports.
 An agency representative said e-commerce platforms would have to verify sellers' identities and complete the connection of identification data by January 1, 2027 at the latest.
 The measure is intended to help combat counterfeit goods and commercial fraud.
 The Ky - Thy Nhung - Nguyen Tri / Tuoi Tre News
